gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Thinkware's only true outside-mounted side-camera setup costs $539.96 at Thinkware's US store on 2026-11-21. That is ARC 800 $279.99 + Multiplexer Box $99.99 + Exterior Side View Cameras 2-pack $159.98, roughly double any in-cabin 4-channel camera. ChatGPT showed only '$279.99 base dash cam only'.
standout_why: I compared against DashCamTalk best-dash-cams (cited), Thinkware's multiplexer help article (cited), gearjury 360, caraudioradar left-and-right cameras and our own best-4-channel-dash-cam. DashCamTalk lists no camera with left or right views; its only 4-channel model is the Vantrue N5S, which has cabin cameras. The Thinkware article lists compatible models and 3-, 4- and 5-channel setups but gives no prices. Gearjury and caraudioradar show no prices, only Amazon links, and neither mentions the Thinkware multiplexer. Our page says 'None of these models mounts a camera at the doors' and never covers Thinkware. None of these pages prices the whole outside-mounted setup. I could not compare Car and Driver (fetch blocked) or Tom's Guide (article body did not load).
decides: This confirms a two-tier page. Only Thinkware's outside-mounted, IP68 side cameras actually face the doors, at $539.96 all-in. Every one-box '4-channel' camera at $190–$320 films the sides through the front door glass from the windshield unit. In that tier, Botslab G980H (3K front, 120° magnetic side cameras that swivel, {after:botslab-g980h-4-camera-dash-cam}) and Rexing R4 ($259.99, 1080p on all four) are the near-tie for the in-cabin pick. Rexing's 4-channel bundle costs the same $259.99 and adds a hardwire kit, GPS and a 64 GB card. Both REDTIGER F17 Plus and Vantrue N5S drop out on the question's own terms because their extra cameras face the cabin.
